title: Climbing Kilimanjaro Over Christmas and New Year
excerpt: Standing on the roof of Africa on New Year's morning sounds special. It is, but it is also the busiest time on the mountain. What to know.
body:
Climbing Kilimanjaro over Christmas and New Year is popular. The weather is often good after the short rains, and many people have time off.

## Weather

The short rains usually fade in early to mid-December. Late December and January are generally dry and clear, with snow on the summit after the rains. Nights are cold at high camp.

## Crowds

This is one of the busiest periods. Campsites on Machame and Lemosho can be full, and summit night can have long lines of headlamps. Quieter options are [Rongai](/blog/kilimanjaro-rongai-route-guide/) and the [Northern Circuit](/blog/kilimanjaro-northern-circuit-guide/).

## Book early

Flights, hotels in Moshi and Arusha and safari lodges fill up fast. We advise booking six to twelve months ahead for this period. See [when to book your safari](/blog/when-to-book-safari/).

## Summit on 1 January?

It is possible to plan for summit morning on New Year's Day. Keep in mind that weather or health can shift plans by a day. Celebrations on the mountain are simple: a song, tea and a lot of hugs.

## Combine it

Christmas on the mountain and New Year on the beach of [Zanzibar](/blog/kilimanjaro-and-zanzibar/) is a popular combination. Read more about [Christmas and New Year in Tanzania](/blog/tanzania-at-christmas/).

[Plan your holiday climb](/travel-proposal/) early.
